title: Indian bonds surge after oil slide eases aggressive rate hike concerns
summary: On Tuesday, Indian government bonds rallied significantly, buoyed by falling oil prices that shifted market sentiment. The 6.94% 2036 bond's yield dipped to 7.2528%, a drop from 7.3169% the previous day. Analysts posit that lower oil prices could relieve inflationary pressure and bolster the rupee, alongside speculation of an upcoming RBI rate hike based on fresh inflation reports.

title: Robust inflows, pullback in shorts lift rupee to seven-month peak

Additionally, traders observed substantial movements in the dollar-rupee non-deliverable forward market as bearish positions were unwound.

title: Nvidia Earnings Preview: 6 key factors investors will watch
summary: Nvidia’s fiscal Q3 2027 earnings report will test the sustainability of the AI boom, with revenue expected to reach $108.9 billion. Investors will scrutinise Data Center growth, hyperscaler demand, Blackwell and Rubin chip rollouts, margins and future guidance, alongside leadership uncertainty and rising costs, to assess its growth outlook.

title: Australia sells A$6 billion of new 2057 Treasury bond
summary: The Australian government's debt management arm made a significant move by issuing A$6 billion in a new Treasury bond set to mature in June 2057, boasting a yield to maturity of 5.62%. With bids totaling A$25.25 billion, investor interest remains strong. The settlement for this issuance is earmarked for November 24, with no additional issuances expected until March 2027. Five prominent banks took lead roles in this offering.

title: Indian bonds gain as oil slide eases rate hike concerns
summary: Indian government bonds saw an increase as oil prices dropped significantly in early trading. This decline in crude prices is expected to ease inflationary pressures and reduce concerns about aggressive rate hikes. The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield fell to 7.2813% during early trading hours. Lower oil prices are particularly beneficial for India, supporting the local rupee and current account deficit.

title: JGB yields climb as buyers hold back on long-dated debt
summary: Japanese government bond yields generally increased on Tuesday except for the benchmark 10-year yield, which fell. The 20-year and 30-year JGB yields reached their highest levels in about a month and since October. Investors are wary of taking interest-rate risks ahead of the 20-year bond auction. Concerns about falling equities may also affect bond supply-demand conditions amidst uncertainty.
